We note that $p=0$ cannot be a solution since division by $0$ is undefined. 

The equation has the denominators $p$ and $6p.$ So first, we find the least common multiple (or $\text{LCM}$) of the denominators. We find that

$$
\text{LCM}(p,6p)=6p.
$$

So, we multiply both sides of the equation by $6p,$ and simplify: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{p+6}{6p}-\frac{2}{p} & =-\frac{p-2}{6p} \\ 6p\cdot (\frac{p+6}{6p}-\frac{2}{p}) & =6p\cdot (-\frac{p-2}{6p}) \\ 6p\cdot \frac{p+6}{6p}-6\cdot p\cdot \frac{2}{p} & =6p(-\frac{p-2}{6p}) \\ \cancel{6p}\cdot \frac{p+6}{\cancel{6p}}-6\cdot \cancel{p}\frac{2}{\cancel{p}} & =\cancel{6p}(-\frac{p-2}{\cancel{6p}}) \\ p+6-12 & =-(p-2)\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $p,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}p+6-12 & =-(p-2) \\ p-6 & =-p+2 \\ 2p & =8 \\ p & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we recall that we cannot allow $p=0$ as a solution. However, since $p=4\ne 0,$ we conclude that the solution is $p=4.$
